tb21_profile.skill: Locate and fetch a 1990s source archive, then make ancient K&R-era C compile and link under a modern gcc/make toolchain and install the binary
tb21_profile.domain: Legacy C / Unix build toolchain: tarballs, hand-written Makefiles, autoconf, gcc diagnostics, /usr/local install prefix, raytracer image output
tb21_profile.task_form: build/packaging from source — download, extract, patch-to-compile, install, verified by running the produced binary

CalibForge.reason: Download GNU Make 3.81 tarball, extract to /app/make-3.81, fix a linker error in old C, install to /usr/local/bin. Same task template.

1992 legacy C base64 tool must be fixed to compile under strict modern flags without touching the Makefile. Same era, same diagnostics.
1998 C library that no longer compiles; repair sources until GCC accepts it, then install. Identical legacy-C repair skill.
Fetch NASM 2.07 source, build, install to /usr/local/bin/nasm, graded by running the binary on a test input. Same fetch-build-run loop.
GNU indent 1.9.1 build dies partway; diagnose the compile failure and finish the install. Old GNU package, modern compiler.
Must locate zip30.tar.gz on SourceForge unaided, then build and install zip 3.0. Trains the find-the-archive half of POV-Ray.
Netpbm from tarball with PNG/JPEG/TIFF delegates; same configure-with-image-libraries build, and output is verified by rendering images.
C project whose build system is broken on this host; repair it, compile, install to /usr/local/bin, tested by running the tool.
libpng 1.0.15 plus zlib and libjpeg all built from source and stacked by prefix — the dependency-ordering part of an old graphics build.

Edit pen.c to remove a planted defect, then compile the package from source and install the executable under a prefix.
Compile a scientific C program from source, modifying the build invocation to get the right executable. Small but same compile-and-install core.
Half-finished C project broken in several ways including the build; repair until it compiles and runs. C build debugging, different subject.

Clone, configure and compile aubio from source before using it. Right shape, but behavioral-only tests make it a weak training signal.

Resolve 'cannot find -lssl / -lcrypto' link failures by fixing library paths and flags. The link-stage failure mode of an old build.
Build OpenSSL from source on Linux: config, make, make install. Same genre; verification is thin (weak).
Write a configure script for a C application, handling feature detection. Teaches what POV-Ray's hand-rolled makefiles are doing.
Fix SQLite linker errors caused by wrong build configuration; adjust the link line until the binary builds.
Source-built OpenSSL installed but the old binary still wins; fix prefix, PATH and ldconfig. The install-actually-took-effect problem.
Install Python 2 from source when no package exists: fetch, configure, make altinstall. Same fetch-build-install chain, weak tests.
Undefined reference to clock_gettime fixed by adding -lrt. Narrow, but it is precisely the missing-library link error class.

VirtualBuildEnv fails to emit deactivate scripts; build-environment shell handling, only loosely connected to compiling C.

Container image build tool defect; build orchestration, far from C compilation.

notes: CalibForge is overwhelmingly the best pool for this task: it contains a whole family of 'build <old package> version <X> from source and install to /usr/local/bin' tasks with pinned-value verifiers, several of which are legacy-C-fails-on-modern-GCC exactly like POV-Ray 2.2. Nine of the final ten are CalibForge and that is the honest answer, not a quota artefact. Terminal-Lego has real build-from-source content (CMake, OpenSSL, custom prefixes, linker errors) but its verifiers are thin — most are weak/ok dominated by file-exists checks — so it never outranks CalibForge. TerminalWorld has the right genre in bulk but its top retrieval hits are almost all FREE; the ten listed came from my own searches and are all ok or better. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is dominated by near-duplicate PostgreSQL-from-source tasks; ranks 8 and 10 are makeweights. SWE-Smith reduces to conan (C/C++ toolchain semantics) and SWE-Rebench to Python packaging — both lose on task_form as expected, and neither belongs in the top 10.
